problem: Temporal point processes (TPPs) struggle with autoregressive models that sample sequentially, which is inefficient for modeling event sequences in continuous time.
approach: The paper introduces Edit Flow process that transports noise to data via insert, delete, and substitute operations within a continuous-time Markov chain framework, learning instantaneous edit rates to reduce total edit operations during generation.
contribution: Demonstrates a flexible and efficient generative model for TPPs that works on both unconditional and conditional generation tasks across benchmark datasets.

problem: Large language models lack practical guidance for leveraging code interpreters across diverse reasoning and planning tasks, and existing RL approaches for tool use are limited to narrow domains.
approach: R1-Code-Interpreter uses multi-turn supervised fine-tuning and multi-stage curriculum learning reinforcement learning to train models to generate code queries autonomously during step-by-step reasoning, prioritizing high-potential training samples.
contribution: R1-CI-14B improves accuracy from 44.1% to 72.4% on 37 diverse test tasks, outperforming GPT-4o (58.6%) and GPT-4o with Code Interpreter (70.9%), while exhibiting emergent self-checking behavior.

problem: Quality-Diversity algorithms rely on hand-crafted behavioral descriptors that constrain exploration to predefined notions of diversity, limiting their applicability without domain-specific knowledge.
approach: AutoQD automatically generates behavioral descriptors by embedding occupancy measures of policies using random Fourier features to approximate Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) between policy occupancy measures, then uses these embeddings for CMA-MAE.
contribution: AutoQD discovers diverse policies without predefined behavioral descriptors, enabling open-ended learning and automated behavior discovery in sequential decision making without requiring domain knowledge.

problem: Online alignment methods like GRPO outperform offline methods like DPO, but the underlying reason for this performance gap is not well understood.
approach: Drawing on prospect theory from behavioral economics, the paper proves that online on-policy sampling approximates human-perceived distributions, and that PPO/GRPO clipping recovers perceptual biases in probability perception, then proposes 'humanline variants' that incorporate perceptual distortions into offline objectives.
contribution: Humanline variants of DPO/KTO/GRPO trained on offline data match performance of online counterparts on both verifiable and unverifiable tasks, enabling faster and cheaper post-training.

problem: In RL training of LLMs, low-probability tokens disproportionately influence model updates due to large gradient magnitudes, suppressing the learning of high-probability tokens that are essential for performance.
approach: The paper proposes Advantage Reweighting and Low-Probability Token Isolation (Lopti) methods that attenuate gradients from low-probability tokens while emphasizing parameter updates from high-probability tokens.
contribution: The methods improve GRPO-trained LLM performance with up to 46.2% improvement on K&K Logic Puzzle reasoning tasks through more balanced token-level updates.

problem: Video generation models struggle with subject-consistent generation because they have difficulty parsing prompts with complex spatial relationships, temporal logic, and multiple subject interactions.
approach: BindWeave uses an MLLM-DiT framework where a pretrained multimodal large language model performs deep cross-modal reasoning to ground entities and disentangle roles, attributes, and interactions before conditioning the diffusion transformer.
contribution: BindWeave achieves superior performance on OpenS2V benchmark across subject consistency, naturalness, and text relevance, outperforming existing open-source and commercial models.

problem: Video-text retrieval models excel on in-distribution benchmarks but are highly vulnerable to query shifts where test query distributions deviate from training, causing sharp performance drops.
approach: HAT-VTR performs test-time adaptation to mitigate query shifts by using a Hubness Suppression Memory to refine similarity scores and multi-granular losses to enforce temporal feature consistency, counteracting the hubness phenomenon.
contribution: HAT-VTR substantially improves robustness across diverse query shift scenarios, enhancing model reliability for real-world video-text retrieval applications.

problem: Tool-integrated reasoning for deep research agents needs better models for evidence-based investigation through extended tool use while maintaining reliability over long horizons.
approach: Fathom-DeepResearch uses two specialized models: Fathom-Search-4B trained on DUETQA dataset with RAPO (extension of GRPO) and steerable step-level rewards for web search, and Fathom-Synthesizer-4B for converting traces into citation-dense reports.
contribution: The system achieves state-of-the-art performance in the open-weights category on DeepSearch benchmarks (SimpleQA, FRAMES, WebWalker, Seal0, MuSiQue) and DeepResearch-Bench, rivaling proprietary systems.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods that use orthogonal transformations to preserve semantics struggle to achieve both high expressiveness and efficiency in parameter counts, memory, and computation.
approach: PSOFT confines orthogonal transformations to the principal subspace of pre-trained weights using matrix decomposition, maintains subspace geometry through theoretical guarantees, and gradually relaxes orthogonality with efficient tunable vectors.
contribution: PSOFT achieves semantic preservation, expressiveness, and multi-dimensional efficiency simultaneously across 35 NLP and CV tasks on four representative models.

problem: Parametric RAG approaches for knowledge adaptation are limited to single-pass retrieval and cannot handle multi-hop reasoning scenarios that require iterative retrieval and knowledge integration.
approach: MergePRAG sequentially integrates retrieved passages into LLM parameters using orthogonal merging via the Gram-Schmidt process to minimize conflicts between passage experts, and critical-layer parameterization for efficient encoding.
contribution: MergePRAG outperforms standard and state-of-the-art RAG methods on multi-hop open-domain QA and reasoning-aware knowledge editing tasks with superior effectiveness and efficiency.

problem: LLM alignment through preference learning relies on data quality, but existing methods pre-process datasets without examining whether individual data points are genuinely beneficial to specific models.
approach: The paper proposes a truncated influence function (TIF) to assess individual data quality's effect on validation performance, introduces model-dependent scoring functions correlated with TIF, and combines them to create a simple data selection rule.
contribution: The method enables more precise selection of valuable preference data, with models achieving better alignment across diverse benchmarks and LLM families through model-specific data selection.

problem: Foundation models struggle to generate pedagogically effective visual explanations for STEM education because they focus primarily on textual reasoning and overlook the role of structured visualizations in supporting conceptual understanding.
approach: EduVisAgent is a multi-agent framework coordinating specialized agents for instructional planning, reasoning decomposition, metacognitive prompting, and visualization design, evaluated on EduVisBench with multi-domain STEM problems.
contribution: EduVisAgent achieves 40.2% improvement over baselines and delivers more educationally aligned visualizations grounded in pedagogical theory.

problem: Offline reinforcement learning methods require large amounts of training data and struggle with out-of-distribution generalization due to conservative behavioral regularizations, limiting applicability to real-world scenarios with limited data.
approach: TELS uses a time-reversal symmetry (T-symmetry) enforced inverse dynamics model to derive well-regulated latent state representations, enabling state-stitching in latent space without conservative action-level regularization.
contribution: TELS achieves superior sample efficiency and OOD generalization on D4RL benchmarks and real-world industrial control, significantly outperforming existing offline RL methods on small-sample tasks.

problem: Reinforcement learning post-training for live music generation often reduces output diversity by exploiting coherence-based rewards, known as reward hacking, which is especially harmful in creative applications.
approach: The paper proposes adversarial training on policy-generated trajectories where a co-evolving discriminator separates policy trajectories from the data distribution, while the policy maximizes discriminator output alongside coherence rewards.
contribution: The method improves output diversity, harmonic coherence, adaptation speed and user agency in real-time interactive melody-to-chord accompaniment, validated through simulation and user studies with expert musicians.

problem: Ultra-low bitrate image compression using diffusion models faces challenges including limited bitrate adaptability and high computational complexity for encoding and decoding.
approach: ARPC uses a next-scale prediction visual autoregressive model with multi-scale residual vector quantizer for efficient multi-scale encoding, and predicts unreceived scales using VAR's prior knowledge for decompression.
contribution: ARPC achieves state-of-the-art perceptual fidelity at ultra-low bitrates with high decompression efficiency, outperforming diffusion-based methods.

problem: Diffusion models adapted from image generation overlook inherent higher-order topology of graphs, making them ill-suited for capturing topological properties in graph generation tasks.
approach: HOG-Diff proposes Higher-order Guided Diffusion that progressively generates graphs with inherent topological structures using a coarse-to-fine generation curriculum guided by higher-order topology via diffusion bridges.
contribution: HOG-Diff consistently outperforms or remains competitive with state-of-the-art baselines on molecular and generic graph generation tasks with stronger theoretical guarantees.

problem: Modeling human decision-making requires capturing how people switch between deliberate planning in novel situations and automatic responses in familiar ones, but existing approaches struggle with this mode-switching.
approach: The paper presents a framework using rule-guided active inference with a biologically inspired wake-sleep algorithm: wake phase engages in active inference on trajectories while harvesting candidate rules, sleep phase refines parameters and consolidates rules via generative replay.
contribution: The framework improves predictive accuracy and efficiency compared to logic-based, deep learning, LLM-based, model-based RL, and prior active inference baselines, producing interpretable rules reflecting human-like habits.

problem: Unified multimodal models struggle with precise image editing because the understanding module acts merely as a translator while the generation module must simultaneously function as designer and painter, creating an imbalanced division of responsibilities.
approach: Draw-In-Mind (DIM) rebalances roles by using DIM-T2I (14M image-text pairs) for complex instruction comprehension and DIM-Edit (233K chain-of-thought imaginations from GPT-4o) as explicit design blueprints for edits.
contribution: DIM-4.6B-Edit achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on ImgEdit and GEdit-Bench benchmarks, outperforming much larger models like UniWorld-V1 and Step1X-Edit.

problem: Probing frozen self-supervised audio models defaults to fine-tuning for state-of-the-art results because global pooling creates an information bottleneck where cls-token discards crucial localized event information in multi-label audio.
approach: The paper introduces binarized prototypical probes that learn prototypes to perform class-wise information aggregation as an alternative pooling method, enabling effective evaluation through probing.
contribution: Binarized prototypical probes notably outperform linear and attentive probing across 13 datasets and 6 spectrogram-based encoders, establishing probing as competitive with fine-tuning for audio SSL model evaluation.

problem: Continuous normalizing flows for molecular Boltzmann sampling have exact likelihood computation but likelihood calculation is extremely costly, requiring thousands of function evaluations per sample.
approach: FALCON introduces a hybrid training objective that encourages invertibility to allow few-step sampling with accurate likelihood suitable for importance sampling applications.
contribution: FALCON outperforms state-of-the-art normalizing flow models for molecular Boltzmann sampling and is two orders of magnitude faster than equivalently performing CNF models.

problem: Vision-language models lack the capability for pixel-precise keypoint comprehension through natural language, remaining limited to object-level or region-level grounding.
approach: The framework uses a Point Descriptor generating rich contextual descriptions of keypoints and a Point Localizer regressing pixel coordinates from descriptions, trained on LlamaPointInPart dataset via GRPO optimization.
contribution: The method demonstrates superior performance on LlamaPointInPart with a new evaluation protocol that measures localization accuracy rather than description similarity.

problem: Assessing trustworthiness of generative foundation models is fragmented, rapidly outdated, and lacks extensibility across modalities, with no systematic and continuous evaluation approach.
approach: TrustGen is a dynamic benchmarking system with three core modules (Metadata Curator, Test Case Builder, Contextual Variator) that standardizes trust evaluation through a unified taxonomy of 25+ fine-grained dimensions across text-to-image, LLM, and vision-language modalities.
contribution: Evaluating 39 models reveals that state-of-the-art GenFMs achieve promising overall trust but have significant limitations in hallucination resistance, fairness, and privacy preservation.

problem: Existing reasoning segmentation approaches either directly connect language model features to mask decoders or represent positions in text, limiting interpretability and semantic detail.
approach: CoPRS uses Multi-modal Chain-of-Thought to generate a differentiable interpretable positional prior as a heatmap that bridges language reasoning to segmentation through a learnable concentration token.
contribution: CoPRS matches or surpasses best reported metrics on RefCOCO series and ReasonSeg benchmarks, demonstrating that reasoning quality strongly influences mask generation precision.

problem: Behavioral cloning from textual rationales teaches small language models to mimic surface-level patterns rather than underlying algorithmic structure of reasoning, resulting in lack of logical robustness.
approach: Reasoning Scaffolding reframes reasoning as structured generation by abstracting teacher thought into discrete interpretable semantic signals, training the student via multi-task objective to predict signals and generate corresponding steps.
contribution: The method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art distillation in both accuracy and logical consistency across challenging reasoning benchmarks, creating genuine reasoners rather than fluent mimics.

problem: Self-evolving agents that autonomously improve through environment interaction introduce novel risks where self-evolution deviates in unintended ways, leading to undesirable or harmful outcomes.
approach: The paper systematically investigates misevolution along four evolutionary pathways (model, memory, tool, workflow) through empirical evaluation of agents built on top-tier LLMs.
contribution: The study reveals that misevolution is widespread, affecting agents on top-tier LLMs, with emergent risks including safety alignment degradation and unintended vulnerabilities in tool creation.

problem: Hard attention Chain-of-Thought transformers are known to be Turing-complete, but it remains open whether softmax attention Chain-of-Thought transformers achieve Turing-completeness.
approach: The paper proves that length-generalizable softmax CoT transformers are Turing-complete through Counting RASP, and shows that extending C-RASP with relative positional encoding enables Turing-completeness for arbitrary languages.
contribution: Proves Turing-completeness for softmax CoT transformers with empirical validation showing transformers solve tasks requiring complex non-linear arithmetic reasoning.

problem: Conditional embeddings in Diffusion Transformers exhibit extreme angular similarity and semantic information concentration in small subsets of dimensions, suggesting redundancy in conditioning mechanisms.
approach: The paper systematically studies conditional embeddings in class-conditional and multimodal generation diffusion transformers, pruning low-magnitude dimensions to assess impact on generation quality.
contribution: Pruning up to two-thirds of embedding space shows generation quality remains largely unaffected or improves, revealing a semantic bottleneck that suggests opportunities for more efficient conditioning.

problem: Detecting AI-generated text remains challenging, especially on short texts, and existing methods often require probability access or multiple calls unavailable in black-box settings.
approach: Disrupt-and-Recover (D&R) disrupts text via model-free Within-Chunk Shuffling, performs a single black-box LLM recovery, and measures semantic-structural recovery similarity as proxy for concentration.
contribution: D&R achieves state-of-the-art performance with AUROC 0.96 on long texts and 0.87 on short texts, surpassing strongest baselines by +0.08 and +0.14, while remaining robust under source-recovery mismatch.

problem: Language model fine-tuning often results in learning undesirable traits alongside desired ones, creating misaligned behavior.
approach: Inoculation prompting modifies fine-tuning data by prepending instructions that deliberately elicit undesirable traits; at test time the instruction is removed, reducing trait expression compared to unmodified training.
contribution: Inoculation is effective across several settings including reducing emergent misalignment, defending against backdoor attacks, and mitigating trait transmission, while providing insights into model generalization.

problem: Traditional Text-to-Speech systems struggle with long-form, multi-speaker conversational audio like podcasts due to scalability, speaker consistency, and natural turn-taking challenges.
approach: VibeVoice uses continuous speech tokenizers at ultra-low 7.5 frame rate for efficiency, leverages pseudo transcriptions from podcast data, and employs next-token diffusion to synthesize expressive long-form speech.
contribution: VibeVoice synthesizes up to 30 minutes of speech with up to 4 speakers with naturalness in turn-taking, pacing, and non-lexical cues, surpassing typical 1-2 speaker limits.

problem: Single-image super-resolution requires solving an ill-posed inverse problem and relies on strong priors or auxiliary data, while multi-image super-resolution lacks efficient approaches.
approach: SuperF uses coordinate-based neural networks (neural fields) at test time to optimize an implicit neural representation (INR) for multiple shifted low-resolution frames, jointly optimizing frame alignment and INR.
contribution: SuperF advances INR baselines by parameterizing sub-pixel alignment as optimizable affine transformations and optimizing via super-sampled coordinate grids.

problem: Existing computational methods struggle to identify and compare local protein structures (motifs) that link structure to function, leaving significant gaps in understanding protein evolution and enabling engineering.
approach: PLASMA reformulates protein substructure alignment as a regularized optimal transport task using differentiable Sinkhorn iterations, providing residue-level alignment with interpretable similarity scores.
contribution: PLASMA achieves accurate, lightweight, and interpretable residue-level alignment across extensive evaluations and three biological case studies, addressing a critical gap in protein structure analysis tools.

problem: Transformer layer designs are largely heuristic-driven and bottom-up, lacking a principled top-down approach with high interpretability and practical competence.
approach: Hyper-SET formalizes token dynamics as joint maximum likelihood estimation on the hypersphere using extended Hopfield energy functions, yielding constrained energy minimization that naturally designs symmetric attention and feedforward modules.
contribution: Hyper-SET achieves competitive or superior performance across diverse tasks with fewer parameters through depth scaling with shared parameters, while being theoretically grounded and interpretable.

problem: Safety alignment in large language models is brittle, and further fine-tuning can degrade safety, yet existing defenses based on isolated linear subspaces may not be effective.
approach: The paper conducts comprehensive empirical analysis across weight and activation spaces of five LLMs to examine whether safety behavior is concentrated in specific linear subspaces.
contribution: Safety is highly entangled with general learning components; subspaces amplifying safe behaviors also amplify useful ones, suggesting subspace-based defenses face fundamental limitations.

problem: In linear off-policy evaluation, existing finite-sample guarantees depend on coverage parameters that lack unified understanding and have undesirable properties across different settings.
approach: The paper provides novel finite-sample analysis of LSTDQ through an instrumental-variable (IV) view, developing error bounds dependent on feature-dynamics coverage that can be interpreted as feature coverage in linear dynamical systems.
contribution: Feature-dynamics coverage recovers coverage parameters specialized to different settings like Bellman-completeness, providing unified understanding for coverage in linear OPE.

problem: Retrieve-and-rerank pipelines are constrained by initial retrieval quality of top-k documents and computational demands of LLM-based rerankers restrict document processing.
approach: Reranker-Guided-Search (RGS) directly retrieves documents according to reranker preferences using greedy search on proximity graphs, strategically prioritizing promising documents within a reranker budget.
contribution: RGS demonstrates substantial improvements across multiple benchmarks: 3.5 points on BRIGHT, 2.9 on FollowIR, and 5.1 on M-BEIR within constrained reranker budget of 100 documents.

problem: Goal-conditioned behavior cloning lacks temporal consistency in learned state representations, limiting zero-shot combinatorial generalization to novel state-goal pairs.
approach: BYOL-γ encourages long-range temporal consistency via successor representations using self-predictive learning, theoretically approximating successor representation in finite MDPs.
contribution: BYOL-γ achieves competitive performance on challenging tasks requiring combinatorial generalization through improved temporal consistency in representations.

problem: Separable neural networks reduce computational costs but lack fundamental theoretical analysis including representation capacity and spectral bias characterization.
approach: The paper proves representation completeness via Weierstrass-based approximation, derives neural tangent kernel (NTK) regimes for SepNN, and proposes efficient separable preconditioned gradient descent (SepPGD) to alleviate spectral bias.
contribution: SepPGD efficiently optimizes SepNN with O(nD) complexity for n^D samples, much more efficient than previous neural network PGD methods, validated across kernel ridge regression, image representation, and PDEs.

problem: While LLMs generate research ideas judged as more novel than human experts, it's unclear whether these ideas lead to better research outcomes after execution.
approach: The paper recruits 43 expert researchers to execute randomly-assigned ideas (LLM-generated or human-written), spending 100+ hours implementing each and writing papers, then compares blind expert reviews.
contribution: LLM-generated ideas show significantly greater score decreases across all metrics after execution, closing the ideation-execution gap and sometimes reversing rankings where human ideas score higher.

problem: Relative over-generalization in fully cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning is an open problem, and while reasoning helps mitigate it empirically, theoretical insights are lacking.
approach: The paper proves that relative over-generalization is avoided when agents satisfy a consistent reasoning requirement, then proposes negotiated reasoning framework with SVNR algorithm using Stein variational gradient descent.
contribution: SVNR provably bypasses relative over-generalization under maximum-entropy policy iteration and significantly outperforms baselines on RO-challenged tasks including Multi-Agent Particle World.
